title: How Financial Firms Work: Business Models and Financial Statements for Supervisors
summary: An eight-module programme helping supervisors understand how financial firms make money, read their accounts and identify capital, liquidity and business model risks.
intro: This training programme equips supervisory staff to understand how financial firms make money, read their financial statements and identify the capital, liquidity and business model risks that matter for supervision.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors a practical understanding of the business models of banks, investment firms, funds, payment firms and crypto-asset firms, and of the financial information that reveals their health. Participants leave able to read a firm's accounts with a supervisory eye, understand capital and liquidity basics and frame the right questions for management.
sections.What It Covers: How different financial firms make money, reading the balance sheet, income statement and cash flow, capital and liquidity basics, group structures and intra-group dependencies, sector-specific risks across banking, investment, funds, payments and crypto-assets, and a business model case workshop.
Intended Audience: New joiners and developing staff in supervisory, authorisation and policy functions
Supervisors and inspectors moving into a new sector or wishing to strengthen their financial analysis
Staff from legal, enforcement or support functions who need to understand firms' business and finances
Learning Objectives: Explain how banks, investment firms, funds, payment firms and crypto-asset firms generate revenue and incur risk
Interpret the main financial statements and identify warning signs of financial weakness
Describe the basic principles of capital and liquidity and why they matter to the authority
Analyse group structures, intra-group dependencies and where risks can be hidden
Identify the key risks for each sector and the supervisory questions they raise
Apply business model analysis to form an initial view of a firm's viability and sustainability
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a four-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a short briefing with worked examples and exercises using realistic financial statements, and modules can be selected or tailored to the sectors the authority supervises.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No accounting qualification is required. Basic numeracy and some familiarity with financial services are helpful.
Core Reading: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (2024), Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (2008), Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision
IOSCO (2017), Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation
FSB (2023), High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Crypto-asset Activities and Markets

modules.title: Business Models: How Financial Firms Make Money
modules.summary: An introduction to business model analysis, the main ways financial firms earn revenue and why supervisors need to understand where profits and risks come from.
objectives: Explain why business model analysis is central to supervision
Identify the main revenue drivers of different types of financial firm
Recognise business models that are unsustainable or depend on excessive risk
syllabus: Interest margin, fees, commissions, spreads and principal risk-taking
Value chains, distribution and dependence on intermediaries
Viability and sustainability: the supervisor's two questions
Signs of a stretched model: rapid growth, outlier returns and concentration

modules.title: Reading Financial Statements with a Supervisory Eye
modules.summary: How to read the balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statement, and how to spot what they reveal and what they conceal.
objectives: Interpret the structure and main lines of the financial statements
Calculate and use basic ratios to assess performance and position
Identify accounting judgements and disclosures that warrant challenge
syllabus: Balance sheet, income statement, cash flow and notes to the accounts
Key ratios: profitability, leverage, cost efficiency and asset quality
Audit opinions, going concern and related party disclosures
Red flags: aggressive accounting, unexplained movements and late filing

modules.title: Capital and Liquidity Basics
modules.summary: The purpose of capital and liquidity requirements, how they are measured and how supervisors judge whether a firm holds enough to absorb losses and meet obligations.
objectives: Explain the purpose of capital and liquidity in protecting customers and markets
Describe how capital requirements and liquidity measures are calculated in outline
Assess whether a firm's capital and liquidity position supports its business plan
syllabus: Loss absorption, quality of capital and own funds
Risk-weighted assets, leverage and fixed overheads requirements in outline
Liquidity risk, funding profiles, buffers and stress
Reading regulatory returns and capital planning

modules.title: Banks and Deposit-Takers
modules.summary: How banks and deposit-takers create credit, manage maturity transformation and earn margin, and the credit, liquidity and concentration risks that most often cause failure.
objectives: Explain maturity transformation, credit creation and net interest margin
Identify the main credit, liquidity and interest rate risks of banks
Frame supervisory questions on lending, funding and asset quality
syllabus: Deposit-taking, lending and the net interest margin
Credit risk, provisioning and non-performing exposures
Funding concentration, deposit runs and interest rate risk
Lessons from recent bank failures for supervisors

modules.title: Investment Firms and Investment Funds
modules.summary: How brokers, asset managers, advisers and funds make money, the role of service providers and depositaries, and the conduct, liquidity and operational risks they carry.
objectives: Distinguish the business models of brokers, managers, advisers and funds
Explain the roles of fund managers, depositaries, administrators and distributors
Identify key risks including client asset, liquidity mismatch and conflict risks
syllabus: Brokerage, execution, asset management and advice revenue models
Fund structures, fees and the fund service provider chain
Client money and assets, liquidity mismatch and valuation risk
Conflicts of interest and the supervisory question set

modules.title: Payment Firms and Crypto-Asset Firms
modules.summary: The business models of payment, e-money and crypto-asset firms, how they earn revenue and why safeguarding, operational and financial crime risks dominate.
objectives: Explain how payment, e-money and crypto-asset firms generate revenue
Assess safeguarding, custody and operational dependency risks
Identify financial crime and consumer harm red flags specific to these sectors
syllabus: Payment flows, interchange, float income and e-money issuance
Crypto-asset exchanges, custody, staking, lending and token issuance
Safeguarding, segregation and the risk of customer shortfalls
Rapid growth, thin capital and dependence on banking partners

modules.title: Group Structures and Intra-Group Risks
modules.summary: How financial groups are organised, why firms sit within wider groups and how intra-group transactions, shared services and parent support affect the regulated entity.
objectives: Map a group structure and identify the regulated entity's position within it
Assess intra-group dependencies, transactions and contagion risk
Frame supervisory questions on group governance and ownership
syllabus: Holding companies, branches, subsidiaries and ownership chains
Intra-group funding, guarantees, outsourcing and shared services
Opaque and complex structures: a supervisory red flag
Group-wide supervision and cooperation with other authorities

modules.title: Business Model Analysis: Case Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a facilitated case in which participants analyse a firm's business model and financial statements and present their supervisory concerns.
objectives: Analyse a firm's business model, financial position and key risks
Prioritise concerns and draft supervisory questions for management
Present and defend an initial view of the firm's viability
syllabus: Case briefing: firm profile, accounts and regulatory returns
Ratio analysis, peer comparison and identifying outliers
Drafting questions for a meeting with the finance director
Workshop: presenting the business model assessment

related.title: Assessing Board Effectiveness
related.summary: An eight-module programme showing supervisors how to assess how a board really works, from papers and decisions to culture and challenge, culminating in case-study interviews.

related.title: Core Supervisory Skills: Business Models, Governance and Risk Governance Panels
related.summary: A three-day workshop taking supervisors from business model analysis through governance interviews to a risk governance panel, using running case studies and role plays.

related.title: Supervising Compliance in Practice: Masterclass Series
related.summary: Ten half-day masterclasses showing supervisors how to test whether firms' compliance arrangements work in practice across core compliance areas.

related.title: Supervisory Risk Assessment Toolkit
related.summary: A ten-module toolkit taking supervisors through the full firm risk assessment cycle, from business model and governance analysis to panels, risk ratings and findings.

related.title: Foundations of Financial Regulation and Supervision
related.summary: An eight-module induction for new regulatory staff covering why we regulate, the authority's powers, risk-based supervision and a first supervisory case.

related.title: Core Professional Skills for Regulatory Staff
related.summary: An eight-module practical programme building the core writing, analysis, meeting, challenge, presentation and data skills that regulatory staff need every day.
